summary: A 43-minute manager coaching session in which Chris Klevan and Ben Byrne screen-share and review the Tim Wigg call recorded the previous day, pausing repeatedly to rework the opening frame, the discovery questions Ben skipped, and how to position a six-month transformation against a cheaper ongoing coach. The second half turns into a full walkthrough of the open-wallet money play, including a worked financial-picture example, the internal payment-plan economics, and when to put the purchase on a credit card. It closes with a discussion of when to challenge a prospect and Chris's own history of over-embellishing a working sales process. Recording disclosure was made on the call.
notable: PAYMENT PLAN ECONOMICS STATED INTERNALLY — Ben asks 'do you know what the total is with the interest if they take the longest payment plan?' and Chris answers 'It would end up being, like, $7,200, because it's $1,200 a month', confirmed by Ben as 'that's six for the six months'. The six-instalment plan therefore carries a 20% uplift over the $6,000 headline. On the two sales calls in this batch where a plan was discussed with a prospect, the disclosure given was only 'a bit of interest' and no total was ever stated.

REPS ARE INSTRUCTED TO CONCEAL THAT PAYMENT PLANS EXIST — 'I don't want to give any sort of inclination that we can do a payment plan. I don't want them to think we can do that until you open wallet them', and reps are to tell prospects 'we don't really have semi-payment plans, it's all custom' specifically because 'it always works to hold the payment plans, because then it gives the open wallet validity'. Standard structured plans plainly do exist.

THE TAUGHT OPEN-WALLET WORKED EXAMPLE IS UNAFFORDABLE ON ITS OWN NUMBERS — the hypothetical prospect discloses $800 a month left after bills and $3,000 available, and the prescribed plan is '$1,200 today and then just continue on with $1,200 a month. That seems like it'd be feasible for you.' The monthly instalment exceeds the disclosed monthly surplus by fifty per cent.

CREDIT CARD FINANCING IS ACTIVELY RECOMMENDED — 'dude, I would put it on the credit card. Here's why. Number one, you're all in... And that's what most people do.' The financial picture script harvests monthly surplus, chequing and savings, number of credit cards, available balance per card, credit score, crypto, stocks and 401k.

The manager's tier-selection heuristic assumes a prospect population the stated ICP explicitly excludes: 'If they have a lot more weight to lose, like they have to lose like 40, 50 pounds, then yeah, I'd probably tell them the 12. If they need to lose like 20 pounds, I'd tell them the six.' The stated ICP says 'It's not like we have dudes who come here who are 50 pounds overweight.'

CLINICAL SCREENING IS ABSENT FROM COACHING — Ben opens by identifying his own failure to probe disclosed pain on the Tim Wigg call: 'he told me all this stuff about pain... I could have actually probed deeper into like, when you say pain, like, where do you feel the pain? How often do you feel it? Like, scale one to 10.' It is framed purely as a missed discovery opportunity. Neither man raises medical screening, contraindication or clinician clearance at any point, here or when discussing another prospect with 'back pain and joint pain'.

Positioning against a cheaper incumbent coach is scripted as a one-time-versus-recurring frame: 'this isn't something where it's like you're going to keep paying as you go... Our goal is that by the end of the six months, you do not need to pay us anymore.' The manager also flags the need to find out what the prospect paid the previous coach: 'there could be a huge difference in the pricing.'

Ben describes the discount and same-day-decision mechanics of a previous, unrelated offer he sold — a $25,000 list price cut to $12,000 on a plan or $10,000 prepaid 'if you make a decision today on this call'. Chris responds that Primal has no such incentive beyond payment-plan interest and the 12-month tier.

The manager openly disagrees with the external mastermind Ben also attends: 'this is the one thing I've heard a lot about Josh Lyons that I don't know if it really serves past a certain point, is this idea that you need to be in the perfect state all the time to close.' Ben is taking coaching from two sources with different doctrines.
Operational detail: cancelled calls show red on the rep calendar, and Ben did not know this until told.
